Senses.Explanation: The mind identified in a record as original or fundamental. The word occurs 748 times in 157 allowlisted texts. The Mirror Record says mind has no form, color, root, lodging, arising, extinction, or observable contemplation; if something observable can be carried out, that text assigns it to reception, conception, activity, and discrimination rather than original mind. The Platform Record pairs recognizing one’s original mind with seeing one’s original nature (若識自本心，見自本性). Other records say it is neither joined nor separate, reject the claim that it first needs stillness, and place original nature and original mind together. These are differing corpus predicates of one textual term, not a menu of interpretations.
Senses.Note: Primary corpus-wide original-mind sense. Cross-check original nature (本性), true mind, and no-mind as neighboring entries with their own predicates. No single imported metaphysical definition is imposed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 心無形色。無根無住。無生無滅。亦無覺觀可行。若有可觀行者。即是受想行識。非是本心。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄). Yongming Yanshou is the exact authorial speaker who distinguishes original mind from observable reception, conception, activity, and discrimination.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲識汝本心非合亦非離
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Buddhanandi section. Buddhanandi is the exact speaker who says that one's original mind is neither joined nor separate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不識本心，學法無益；若識自本心，見自本性
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Record of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經). Huineng is the exact speaker who pairs recognizing one's original mind with seeing one's original nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 本心不寂要假寂靜。本來寂故何用寂靜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Bodhidharma biography. Bodhidharma is the exact quoted speaker who rejects the claim that original mind first requires stillness.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖祖佛佛只說如人。本性本心別無道理。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Lao'an section. Lao'an is the exact speaker who places original nature and original mind together and says there is no other principle.

Senses.Explanation: A person’s prior intention or purpose. Guizong Yirou says, “this day’s affair was not my original intention” (此日之事，故非本心) and immediately explains that he had not intended even to reside on a mountain. In a succession discussion Fushi Yigong says that nobody had accorded with his original intention except Mingyuan (無有契我本心者). These event and decision contexts refer to intention, not original mind.
Senses.Note: Ordinary intention sense. Copies of the same “this day’s affair” event in several compilations were treated as one transmitted witness. The phrase “depart from original mind/intention” was excluded because its referent is ambiguous.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大眾，此日之事，故非本心。實謂祇箇住山寧有意，向來成佛亦無心。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Guizong Yirou section. Guizong Yirou is the exact speaker who says that the day's affair was not his original intention and explains that he had not intended to reside on a mountain.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我雖則繼席六載，無有契我本心者，惟明元隨我十餘年
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fushi Yigong (伏獅義公禪師語錄), succession discussion. Fushi Yigong is the exact speaker who says that nobody except Mingyuan accorded with his original intention.
